explanation: Fires on existential 'there'/'There' as the subject of 'there is/are/was/will be/must be' constructions, especially after a clause boundary or a connective (however, so, for example, and, yet). Locative 'there', 'here' and 'thereupon' get weak to moderate activation.

Fires on a word-internal subword fragment, usually the first piece after the opening of a word that gets split into several tokens. Common cases are 'pl' in plasmid/plasmon/plies/plazo, 'og' in hypoglycemic/normoglycemia, 'G' in Gastro and pieces of names (Nor-, Cong-, Melksh-). Whole common words rarely fire, and code tokens fire only weakly.

Fires on short word-initial fragments of words split into pieces, often after a hyphen or period: '-h' in pull-hitter, hard-hitting and NTLM-hashed, 'hal' in halts, 'há', '.p12', '.n'ovell, 'T' in 99mTc. A grab-bag of mid-word and hyphen-attached subword tokens. Numbers and ordinary words fire weakly.

Fires on deictic or emphatic words in conversational speech that point at something here and now: 'over' in 'over there', 'right' in 'right there/right now/that's right/right?', 'look at this', 'up there', 'here I am'. Sentence-final periods and formal text give only weak activation.

Fires on tokens in phrases about long or short duration, size or form (e.g. 'for a few weeks', 'for a long', 'short stories', 'unsigned char/short'), usually on the article or word just before the length/size expression. Also fires on some unrelated tokens such as a URL path piece and sentence-initial 'The'/'In'.

Fires on the first content token of a new document or section, especially in boilerplate or headers: license/copyright headers (OpenSSL, Microsoft, LICENSE, BEGIN LICENSE BLOCK), the start of a code file (import, sqlite), the start of an article or abstract, and the broken 'µ'/degree characters before 'years' in scientific text. Activation is weaker later in running prose.

Fires mostly on physics and quantum-science terms in scientific abstracts ('quantum', cavity-QED, 'time' in time-of-flight/real-time, Dzyaloshinskii, multidimensional). It also fires on word-middle subword fragments of other technical or proper words (bipolar, nulliparous, Homespun, Molot).

Fires on the last subword piece of a long, multi-token technical word or proper name (fructofuranose, Sinding-Larsen, Chillicothe, Collenchyma, plasmacytoma, Condensate, PodsCondensed, 'station' in a railway-station name). Activation is weak on short common words.

Fires on function or connective tokens inside fixed formulaic phrases where the next words are highly predictable: 'the same is true', 'as the case may be', 'LICENSE_1_0.txt or copy at', 'or not', 'U.S. Atty', and 'Kansas', 'Pakistan' or 'New Hampshire' completing a known place or party name. Mainly about predictable phrase completion, with mixed surface forms.

Fires on words in descriptions of a concrete physical action or a situation in progress, often a preposition or conjunction tying an action to what happens at the same time ('when', 'while', 'as', 'keep hold of', 'hand on', 'eat with', 'tape drive', 'gaze'). Diffuse, with no consistent token identity.

Fires mainly on citation markup in scientific text: the '[@' token opening a reference after '(' or '\[', leading zeros in reference IDs (bib0020, bb0005), and 'p' in p-value statements. A few unrelated tokens also fire ('a' in 'at a rate', 'bonding', 'trans').

Fires strongly on two separate things: (1) forms of the verb 'come'/'came' (come across, came from, came up with, come with, came to see), and (2) subword pieces inside medical or biological compound words (immun-os-uppressive, lymph-ob-lastic, melan-oc-ortin, immun-om-odulatory). Assorted other tokens fire too.

Fires on content words or subword pieces in medical and technical descriptions, plus prepositions inside formal phrases ('Judge for the District', 'across a wireless channel', 'oxygenation to'). There is no clear shared feature across Spanish 'y', disease names, 'robots' and 'lifestyle'.

Fires on the head noun of a compound or set term that names a structured item, field or category, such as 'POINTS' in REFERENCE POINTS, 'cycles', 'Tasks', 'Tax Return', 'executionOrder', 'design', 'caption', 'feed', 'schedule', 'Date' in forms. This is the second element of a label-like noun phrase, often a metadata or record field name.

Fires on the main verb right after 'to', a modal or a negation, especially in infinitive purpose or question constructions ('How to access', 'to monitor', 'reorganize', 'can't escape', 'help educators celebrate'). Copular and auxiliary verbs (be, become, were) fire only weakly.

Fires on words about the surroundings, the periphery or an external relation: 'side' (side-effects, side project), 'surround', 'around', 'above' in 'link above', 'external site', 'new site', 'extern', 'ambient', 'near'. Roughly about location relative to something external or secondary.

Fires on a word that completes a contrast or a correction of expectation, where the text sets X against a contrasting alternative ('E-selectin' vs P-selectin, 'domestically' vs abroad, 'chloroquine' as the alternative, 'does not' vs another case, 'Cython'). Also fires on assorted subword word endings, so the signal is mixed.

Fires on the preposition 'to' when it marks a recipient, target or direction after a verb or noun ('chained himself to', 'delivered to', 'make sense to me', 'supplied to', 'kick to', 'access to', 'extent to which'). Infinitival 'to' and other words give little activation.

Fires on parts of technical or proper named entities, particularly software, domain or command tokens: '.org'/'.com' in URLs, launchpad, SteamOS, 'git pull/branch', 'apt-get install', MSBuild, 'TLSv', 'Champions League', 'Society of Automotive Engineers'. These are completions of well-known multi-token names.

Fires on structural tokens that start the next segment: the '.\n' ending a paper title just before the abstract begins, the ':' after 'type' in code, '@' in JSDoc '@param', 'at' and 'to' in GPL license boilerplate, and articles or verbs in the middle of sentences. Broadly about predictable boundary or template positions, but heterogeneous.

Fires inside biological species and organism names and the prepositions linking them in microbiology or biology text: 'occus' in Streptococcus, 'rio' in Vibrio, 'T' in TTV, 'of'/'in'/'by' just before a species name (strains of L. lactis, in Arabidopsis, by Clostridium). Generic words in other domains fire weakly.
